children: Increases in Chinese and European aluminum output won't be enough to pull the global market out of deficit this year, says Commonwealth Bank of Australia's Vivek Dhar. However, rising supply from India and Indonesia, alongside an anticipated recovery in Middle East supply, is expected to flip the aluminum market into surplus next year, Dhar says. "This should fundamentally weigh on aluminum prices--especially if the U.S. dollar strengthens as we anticipate in the coming quarters," he says in a note. Dhar estimates 55%-60% of the volume lost from Middle East supply disruptions has been offset by Chinese production growth between January and August. Stronger European output has offset another roughly 20% of those supply interruptions, he says. (rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com; @RhiannonHoyle)
